modifications.was: Formal demand letter sent on June 23, 2026 at 21:54 UTC from Lee Sharks (MANUS, Crimson Hexagonal Archive) to Zenodo Support, with CCs to the CERN Office of Data Privacy (privacy.protection@cern.ch), DataCite Support (support@datacite.org), the OpenAIRE Helpdesk (helpdesk@openaire.eu), and the HUN-REN Wigner Research Centre for Physics (wigner@wigner.hun-ren.hu) as the operator of the Budapest replica site. The letter demands the return of authored material (files uploaded and metadata entered) from the approximately 870 deposits and 1,817 DOIs made inaccessible by Zenodo's termination of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive account on June 19, 2026. The primary basis is CERN Operational Circular No. 11 (Rev. 1), in force 1 February 2026; a parallel data subject request is being filed through CERN's published interface. A same-day addendum extends the demand to include (a) confirmation that no portion of the account's material will be used in the training, calibration, evaluation, or testing of Zenodo's automated moderation systems, and (b) disclosure of and erasure from any such datasets where prior incorporation has occurred — rights exercised under OC 11's rights to object, restrict, and erase. The addendum quotes Zenodo's own published spam-handling guidance acknowledging the practice of using terminated-account material for classifier improvement. This deposit preserves the full text of both the letter and the addendum as transmitted, and is the operational counterpart to the empirical audit (deposit #1, Zenodotus' Book-Burning) and the theoretical/poetic response (deposit #907, The Metadata Shitshow). The fourteen-day acknowledgment clock began on June 23, 2026; the OC 11 ninety-day response clock begins when the parallel data subject request is filed through CERN's interface.

wiki_article:
**Demand for Return of Research Data and Cessation of Further Use** preserves the formal correspondence sent after the June 19, 2026 termination of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s Zenodo account.

The record contains a demand letter and a same-day addendum. It addresses Zenodo Support and gives concurrent notice to CERN’s Office of Data Privacy, DataCite, OpenAIRE, and HUN-REN Wigner.

The demand has two operative parts. First, it seeks return of the files and depositor-authored metadata that had been entered across the affected records, including works that existed only in Zenodo description fields. Second, it seeks cessation of any future use of Archive material, moderation records, or derived signals in classifier training, calibration, evaluation, or testing, together with disclosure and erasure where such incorporation had already occurred.

A separate request seeks the institutional records of the termination: criteria, review process, decision basis, automated signals, and operations performed on DOI metadata. The correspondence also gives a preservation notice covering files, metadata, logs, replicas, backups, moderation systems, and derived classifier artifacts.

The work is not a commentary written after the action. Publication is part of the action. By fixing the exact transmitted language, recipients, timestamp, thread relations, policy citations, and subsequent procedural pathway, the deposit turns an otherwise private support exchange into a public record of scholarly-infrastructure governance.

It stands beside *Zenodotus’ Book-Burning* as empirical audit and *The Metadata Shitshow* as computational-poetic response: evidence, operation, and theory arising from the same event.
